items.title: Share these readings with your care team
items.text: Only 58.8% of your readings were in the 70-180 range (weeks 11-12); the usual target is more than 70%. Your average was 181.9 mg/dL. Bring this to your next visit.

rejected.text: You had readings in the 70-180 range only 58.8% of the time, which is lower than the target of more than 70%. Bring this to your next visit to discuss your average reading of 181.9 mg/dL.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal went with a smaller rise in sugar, about 3.2 mg/dL smaller in one study and 18.3 mg/dL smaller in another. Walking 10 to 19 minutes after dinner got most of the gain, with a rise 17.5 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: Most of your dinners, 58.3%, started at 8 pm or later, which went with a rise in sugar about 9.2 mg/dL more than earlier dinners. Try to start dinner before 8 pm, as sugar rose about 13.3 mg/dL more after a dinner at 8-9 pm than after one before 6 pm.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 12.1 hours, with 25.0% of nights reaching 13 hours. Adding an overnight fast to coaching changed the outcome by -0.03 points compared to coaching alone in one program.
